not: A ceremony framework: every mechanism must prevent a real failure worth its cost.
A second source of truth beside Git.
An engine that invents human decisions or acts without authority.
A deploy, CI or release-publishing tool: its release support is a branching strategy.
Inherently opinionated: it ships an opinionated default graph, but every opinion (graph, lenses, prompts, policy) can be customised by the project.
principles: Git is the store; state is visible and repairable by hand.
A small engine; the graph, prompts and policy belong to the project.
Human authority is explicit: approvals may be delegated, but decisions with big consequences go to the owner, batched.
Reviews are independent, and a finding must matter.

Guard against drift at both levels: from what a goal asked for, and from the project's original intent. A goal that departs from the project's intent is flagged when it is added, and the owner either changes the goal or amends the intent.
Prefer deleting to adding; keep prompts distilled.

spec:
Rewrite docs/WHITEPAPER.md as an accessible conceptual/design paper introducing deterministic progressive disclosure as a general architectural idea for agentic software. Immediately define it in the first substantive sentence: deterministic software selects which information and instructions to disclose to an agent according to explicit inputs and rules, rather than leaving the disclosure decision to the agent's own reasoning. Inputs may include user choices, external results or workflow state; ZzzOps is one application, not the definition or limit of the concept. Explain how ZzzOps uses it to give agents clear instructions for progressing through a defined workflow.

The latest owner feedback supersedes the earlier implementation-audit emphasis, exhaustive behavioral inventory, technical-back-half requirement and approximate 5,000–7,000 word target. The central contribution is the philosophy and architecture. Use the structure and tone of an accessible scientific concept paper: definition-led abstract, motivation/problem, proposed concept and design principles, illustrative ZzzOps application, discussion/trade-offs and conclusion. Explain unfamiliar terms when introduced, favor connected plain prose and a small illustrative example over dense tables, schemas, command references or implementation jargon. Simplify further wherever explanation can be shorter without losing the central idea; no minimum word target. Do not invent experimental results or empirical claims merely to mimic an experimental paper. Apply consulted scientific-writing guidance: one central contribution, clear terms and motivation, logical progression, accessible abstract, and bounded claims.

Make the mostly unopinionated engine and opinionated configurable layer a central architectural philosophy. Explain a generic engine's stable execution/state invariants separately from a repository-owned, customizable directed acyclic graph (define DAG in plain language), policies, prompts, review steps and approval choices. ZzzOps ships an opinionated default workflow; repositories can change that workflow. Mostly unopinionated does not mean assumption-free or that engine invariants can all be configured away. Explain why this separation is useful, its costs, and how it supports deterministic disclosure. Also develop the supported philosophies of explicit coordination versus agent judgment, durable work beyond a chat, visible human authority, and critique/correction, only as they support the central idea.

The latest owner request supersedes mandatory evidence-ledger, size-reproduction and checker requirements: remove bulky public evidence material, retaining only a minimal checked-source/version/reference note or links to SPEC/DESIGN where helpful. Refresh design and test_design to retire or simplify the frozen manual checker as appropriate; tooling must not dictate reader-facing content. Add no new verification infrastructure, wording tests or CI hooks. Prefer existing normative SPEC/DESIGN links over reproducing implementation mechanics. No runtime, policy, template, schema or contract changes. Align the README link with the revised conceptual framing. Preserve David Rzepa byline and agent drafting/review disclosure, brief generic positioning/related approaches without unsupported superiority or historical-first claims. No dogfood report, private evidence, evaluation, benchmarks or external publication required. Unsupported reliability/cost benefits remain hypotheses/design aims. Respect existing gates; GitHub currently blocks PR #773 under the dev rules, so do not weaken rules to merge.

Owner feedback, verbatim:
"Immediately define ¨Deterministic progressive disclosure¨. This is not a concept specific to zzzops, it could be used for any agentic software. The idea is that instead of the agent driving the disclosure, deterministic software drives the disclosure based on some input. The describe how zzzops uses it to ensure that agents are given clear instruction about how to move through the defined workflow."
"The overall tone doesn't seem like a paper introducing a new concept or idea. I'm not sure how to describe it, but it's way off. Look up guidance on how to write scientific papers and adjust the tone. I'm struggling to understand it. I think it could be less technical so a wider audience can parse it. It doesn't need to describe zzzops in excruciating detail either, the most important part is the philosphies it's built on"
"We need to explicitly describe the philosophy that the engine is mostly unopinionated and the actual workflow DAG is customizable. It's an interesting concept to build software with an unopinionated and an opinionated layer."

This continues G1036 and PR #773; preserve existing design/review history and refresh the design through the ordinary goal workflow. The user's existing standing approval delegation persists; genuinely new owner decisions still go to the owner.

Latest owner feedback, verbatim (supersedes earlier evidence and depth requirements):
"Ok much better. One thing that isn't explained is that the frontier provides multiple target actions, so it supports parallelisation and model selection for specific tasks (I don't remember if we actually implemented that after the design reset, but we can suggest its useful for that) I think we can simplify even further, I'm honestly not sure how useful the evidence is. And we could add a Future Work section with more ideas for uses for the concept."

Explain the frontier as a set of eligible actions, not a single next action. Source verification confirms that render.goal_actions/render_next expose multiple eligible actions, capacity and per-action capability; card.run.models is selected from repository settings.routing.tiers. These support independent parallel tasks and task-specific model choices; actual dispatch and model choice are performed by the root/harness, and fully automated routing is proposed future work. Add a concise Future Work section with clearly proposed general applications such as parallel orchestration/task-model routing, research/evidence workflows, state-adaptive user-facing assistants and human decision handoffs. Preserve the general immediate definition, accessible conceptual tone, and central mostly unopinionated engine/customizable opinionated workflow-layer architecture. Align README. Keep existing local verification and GitHub approval gates; no runtime or repository policy changes.

Latest owner steering, verbatim (supersedes WD3/WD4 blog deliverable):
"I think the whitepaper needs more of an introduction to ZzzOps - what it is. It just jumps right into it at the moment, assuming the reader knows. Also, we don't need the blog post .md."

At the start of the ZzzOps illustration, add a concise introduction for readers unfamiliar with it: repository-based goal and release management for coding agents, whom it serves, durable goals across sessions, coordination of workers/reviews/checks/human decisions. Explain release support as branching and merge coordination rather than deployment. Then continue the existing architecture discussion. Remove docs/blog/release-1.md and any operative blog-draft requirements or references in the design, README and PR description. Prior WD3/WD4 owner quotes may remain as historical decisions only with this explicit supersession. Keep this a small focused editorial revision and preserve all existing review/check and GitHub gates; no new infrastructure/runtime/policy edits.

Additional owner requirement, verbatim:
"A Prior Work section about progressive disclosure and any other similar concepts (including if there's existing work like determinstic progressive disclosure)"

Fold a concise substantive Prior Work section into the same pending introduction/blog-removal revision. Conduct actual primary-source web research on established progressive-disclosure HCI usage, staged agent context/loading and explicit software workflow/context selection. Search the exact phrase deterministic progressive disclosure and close variants; report any credible prior usage with bounded search caveats, never historical-first/novelty/superiority claims from non-discovery. Open/read cited original sources and distinguish who selects disclosure. Explain overlap and differences accessibly with direct primary citations. A short selective comparison is sufficient; no exhaustive survey or new infrastructure. All preceding accepted conceptual structure, latest ZzzOps introduction and blog removal remain in scope.
